title: SAFE-Teen: Evaluating Chatbot Safety Across Adolescent Mental Health Conversations
abstract: arXiv:2611.07218v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Adolescents are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, advice, and companionship, raising safety concerns. While recent evaluations have started to examine safety across multiple conversational turns, few compare how slight changes in a teen's responses can affect a chatbot's safety in the same scenario. We conduct a clinician-informed evaluation of chatbot safety in simulated conversations with adolescents aged 13-17, examining how safety failures vary with adolescents' responses and teen-aware system prompting. We evaluated 32,555 simulated conversations across 18 chatbot APIs and two system-prompt conditions using 22 safety criteria grounded in previously identified harms. Conversations spanned 983 variants of 106 seed scenarios covering urgent safety issues, health advice, and identity and relationships. translated_title: SAFE-Teen：评估青少年心理健康对话中聊天机器人的安全性
translated_abstract: 青少年越来越多地求助于AI聊天机器人以获取心理健康支持、建议和陪伴，这引发了安全方面的担忧。尽管近期的评估已开始检验多轮对话中的安全性，但很少有研究比较青少年在同一场景中回应的细微变化会如何影响聊天机器人的安全性。我们对13-17岁青少年的模拟对话开展了一项由临床医生指导的聊天机器人安全性评估，考察安全失败如何随青少年回应的变化以及青少年感知型系统提示而变化。我们基于先前已识别的危害制定了22项安全标准，在18个聊天机器人API和两种系统提示条件下评估了32,555个模拟对话。对话涵盖了106个种子场景的983个变体，涉及紧急安全问题、健康建议以及身份认同与人际关系。在没有青少年感知提示的条件下，总体安全标准失败率为43.3%，而在启用该提示的条件下则为24.9%。
tldr: 该研究通过基于22项安全标准、覆盖18个聊天机器人API的32,555个模拟青少年心理健康对话，揭示了青少年回应的细微变化会显著影响聊天机器人的安全性，且青少年感知型系统提示可将总体安全失败率从43.3%降至24.9%。
en_tdlr: This study conducts a clinician-informed evaluation of chatbot safety in adolescent mental health conversations, using 32,555 simulated dialogues across 18 chatbot APIs and 22 safety criteria, revealing that slight variations in teen responses significantly affect safety outcomes, and that teen-aware system prompting reduces the overall safety failure rate from 43.3% to 24.9%.
